articles.summary: Carson Hocevar leads NASCAR merchandise sales and has a TikTok girlfriend, but Denny Hamlin and Kevin Harvick say he needs to focus on racing.
articles.body: Carson Hocevar isn't your typical NASCAR driver. He's not your daddy's driver. He's certainly not your granddaddy's driver. He's no Dale Earnhardt. He's not Richard Petty or Cale Yarborough or, for those looking for a more recent driver, Tony Stewart. In a way, he's probably the closest thing to Jeff Gordon we've had since ... Jeff Gordon. CARSON HOCEVAR SAYS HIS MOM WAS MORE FIRED UP ABOUT HIM GOING TO THE MET GALA THAN WINNING AT TALLADEGA Hocevar, 23, is rewriting the rules in just about every single way. He's only got one career Cup win — earlier this year at Talladega (hey, maybe he is Dale!) — but is currently leading the series in merchandise sales. Last year, he wasn't even in the Top 30. When I told my wife I was interviewing Carson Hocevar earlier this week, I expected her to look at me like I had three heads. "Oh, I know him," she said. "From TikTok." "I just kind of laugh about it," Hocevar said about all the attention — both good and bad — he's getting from a suddenly vibrant social media presence. "You know, the night before Talladega, I was six hours away at my buddy's place driving $500 cars, and then we win the next day. So, you know, it's always ... you just put yourself in that spot sometimes that I think in racing, when people just want to have a reason for stuff, they don't want to just be like, 'Oh, circumstance, you know?' "They just want to dictate a reason or, you know, push a story or whatever." Carson Hocevar and his "TikTok girlfriend" Hocevar's popularity, both within the sport and outside of it, has exploded this summer. In July, social media sleuths started linking him to popular influencer, Tabitha Swatosh. Swatosh has over 15 million followers on TikTok, and unleashed a video last month that tallied nearly 500,000 likes. "A NASCAR man invited me to be his date to an event," she said in the video before showing all 15 million followers how she gets ready for said event. Side note: No, I don't get it. Don't ask me why people watch what they watch on TikTok. I have no clue. I'm not the target audience, though. Anyway, fast-forward a few weeks, and the two were spotting together on the starting grid before the Brickyard 400. Pretty easy to connect the dots after this: Which brings us to August, where Carson finished 31st, 37th, 19th and, after a late crash last Saturday at Daytona, 38th. Not great! Add in some off-the-track drama around Swatosh after she "wore heels to a race," which apparently didn't sit well with some fans, and it's been a rocky summer for Hocevar. Too much TikTok girlfriend and not enough practice in the simulator? Well, if you ask championship favorite Denny Hamlin ... "I don't know. It just was not a very good day," Hamlin said about Hocevar on his 'Actions Detrimental' podcast following a wreck at New Hampshire. "The best thing that's come out of that camp in a month is his girl's tutorial on makeup and racing." Whoooooooof. Hamlin wasn't alone. "Here’s how it goes a lot of times when you see a young driver that gets a lot of attention, had some success, wins a race," former Cup champion Kevin Harvick said last week. "Got a TikTok girlfriend. All these things that go along with all that, and then they forget that they need to drive the freaking race car. "The guy can drive the crap out of the race car, and all the other stuff is really cool ... No one cares if your car is not fast. It does not matter if you don’t have the results. "They will forget about you in weeks." NASCAR is pushing Carson Hocevar, for good reason There's certainly some truth to that. Fans want to root for a winner. Hocevar told me as much when I spoke to him earlier this week. But if you win, and nobody knows anything else about you, that probably won't last, either. "A lot of my friends love the WWE and they they were reading the WWE Reddit, and they're in some of the comments and they thought they accidentally switched to the NASCAR Reddit by accident because the fans over there kind of say the same stuff they do over here," Hocevar said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "They don't understand the new guys. 'This guy is popular, and I don't understand why.' A lot of my friends, some of them love WWE and all the intricacies of that world. But the casuals of it, they're like, 'Man, I loved Stone Cold when he walked out. I never even watched him wrestle, but I liked him, and the Undertaker and their shticks. "It's very similar to how NASCAR fans describe everything and become negative to everything. A lot of times, they're not sure what they're looking for." NASCAR, by the way, is sure what it's looking for. The series has been pushing Hocevar over the past few weeks in a way we haven't seen ... maybe ever? Last Thursday, the series sent out a press release titled, "Does Everyone Hate Carson Hocevar?" It was odd. You don't see that in this business. The story made sure to note that Hocevar is currently No. 1 driver in retail sales on the NASCAR Shop website, and ranked inside the top five of trackside sales. He was No. 32 this time last season. "Love him or hate him, Carson Hocevar is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore … so catch him and all his enemies this Saturday night, Aug. 29, during the Coke Zero Sugar 400," the article concluded. So, yeah — NASCAR isn't oblivious to this. They're very clearly pushing Carson Hocevar to the center of the table, and letting the chips fall where they may. There's a reason I spoke to Carson earlier this week. I didn't ask. He was offered. That also doesn't happen often. It's not the worst strategy in the world. Every sport needs a villain. A lightning rod. Someone who's going to move the needle. NASCAR, in particular, has been desperate for that driver for a decade now. Jeff Gordon retired in 2015. Tony Stewart retired in 2016. Dale Earnhardt Jr. retired in 2017. Kyle Busch, sadly, died in May. He was undoubtedly the most polarizing driver in the sport for years. His death rocked the series in more ways than one. So now, apparently, it's Carson Hocevar's turn. He's got the TikTok girlfriend, as Kevin Harvick said. The social media presence. Plenty of enemies on the track. He's also got a shot at winning a Cup championship in a few months. The only thing left to do? Win. "I think we'll just enjoy these (next) ten (races) and keep working and, you know, just see where it works out."

articles.title: Antonelli saldrá último en Monza y no se descarta: "No tengo presión, ganar sería increíble"
articles.standfirst: El italiano es un foco de atención claro en su carrera de casa y con el Mundial en una situación idílica
articles.summary: El italiano es un foco de atención claro en su carrera de casa y con el Mundial en una situación idílica
articles.body: E n el Parco di Monza, un lugar emblemático entre el que hay parques, actividades... y un circuito, todavía no se escuchan rugir motores, pero una marabunta peregrina para visitar al hombre llamado a devolver a su bandera, la tricolor de Italia, a lo más alto de la Fórmula 1. Cada vez es más real que Andrea Kimi Antonelli, el segundo más joven de la piloto, pueda acompañar a Nino Farina y Alberto Ascari como campeón del mundo para el país transalpino. Llega con 59 puntos de renta y el cielo es el límite. Hasta la sanción al introducir la nueva unidad de potencia de Mercedes parece perder peso real cuando se trata del piloto boloñés. Saldrá último en las largas rectas, pero nadie le quiere destacar. "¿Cómo acabará? Pues podio. Hay muchas rectas y será feliz", decía Fernando Alonso respecto al italiano. Y el líder de la Fórmula 1 viene sin presión, no tiene nada que perder. "Me quita presión... y me haría mucha ilusión ganar. Me subiré al coche con la mente despejada y voy a disfrutar, pero el objetivo es sacar el mejor resultado", reconocía. Una actitud diferente. Aunque también realista. "Un buen resultado sería un top-5, pero depende de tu ritmo y sabemos que Ferrari, McLaren o Red Bull estarán muy cerca", añadió. Antonelli juega con la presión, algo que sí le ha golpeado cuando venía a Monza. Allí debutó en sesión oficial en 2024 y estrelló el Mercedes y en 2025 vivió un fin de semana horrible. Ahora la cosa cambia. "Estoy liberado de presión, aunque preferiría la pole. Pero voy a poder disfrutar más, es una nueva oportunidad y un método de trabajo diferente", lanzó. En esa búsqueda de un buen fin de semana también puede tener relación con una Mercedes fuerte y jugarán con la carta del trabajo en equipo. Si en Holanda se vio a Russell ayudar, en Italia puede ser parecido con los rebufos. "Lo haré si me lo piden. Lo hemos hablado y acordamos varias cosas, pero dependerá de cómo se desarrolle la sesión. Haré todo lo posible para ayudar al equipo", confesó. Aunque su remontada abre un escenario diferente y un Mundial que puede abrirse. La competencia es total. "Nos puede sentar bien este circuito, pero sabemos lo fuerte que es McLaren, Ferrari estará en lo más alto e incluso Red Bull. Pero tenemos en cuenta que nuestro coche sigue siendo muy competitivo pese a no tener grandes mejoras desde Canadá", cerró. Su sonrisa no se borra. Un Kimi más relajado ha llegado para quedarse.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli: Mercedes driver plays down speculation around future switch to Ferrari ahead of Italian GP
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli goes into his home race at the top of the Drivers' Championship; the Italian responded to speculation that he could drive for Ferrari later in his career; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
The 20-year-old Italian has exceeded all expectations to lead the Drivers' Championship by 59 points after 12 rounds of just his second season in Formula 1.

Antonelli's superb 2026 form has seen his popularity grow massively in Italy, creating a potential dilemma for the home fans at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix who would usually be loyal to Ferrari.

Asked about expectations that he could join Ferrari later in his career, Antonelli said: "Being an Italian myself, I know how emotional we are and how excited we can get about things. Sometimes overly excited.

"Of course, there will always be this kind of talk but, at the end of the day, as much as Ferrari is massive, incredible brand, I am very happy where I am.

"I am very happy with Mercedes because they are the ones who have given me the opportunity since I was a kid and I feel like I have so much to give back to them. Got to live with that."

Antonelli open to Verstappen-Red Bull longevity

Antonelli was later asked for his views on Max Verstappen's recent decision to sign a contract extension with Red Bull, who similarly signed the Dutchman as a teenager.

Verstappen was 17 when he was given a drive at Red Bull's then junior squad Toro Rosso in 2015, before promoted into the senior team during the following season.

The 2026 season is Verstappen's 10th full campaign with Red Bull, and Antonelli foresees a similar future for himself with Mercedes.

"I think Max has an incredible relationship with Red Bull," Antonelli said. "Also, they were the one to put him in a car at a very young age. They were the one to put the trust.

"I feel like he's happy in the team, from what I can see. And he probably feels like wanting to stay with them. He probably believes as well in this project. So, I think he has all the reasons and all the rights to stay with Red Bull.

"And if one day he wants to change, then it's going to be up to him. But as long as he's happy where he is, why not?

"I will do the same with Mercedes is. I feel like I have, first of all, so much to give them. And if I will be happy all throughout with them, I will probably stay with them for my whole career as well.

"So, let's see. Of course, you never know what can happen."

Despite it being Antonelli's home race, Mercedes have chosen Monza as the circuit for Antonelli to receive a grid penalty for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.

Two separate engine problems earlier in the year made it inevitable Antonelli would have to take a penalty at some point, and Monza is viewed as one of the tracks where it's easiest to fight through the field from the back of the grid.

"In some ways it helps to release pressure, although I [would] very much rather fight for pole and start at the front," Antonelli said.

"But, in some ways, I feel like it makes me a bit more relaxed going into the weekend and that's why I am going to able to enjoy more the driving and the weekend itself.

"Of course, it's as well a different opportunity, an opportunity to try something different during the weekend. A different work method in free practice especially because we have the chance to do so.

"I think it's going to be a very interesting weekend."

Mercedes had previously explained that the decision had the potential to relieve pressure on Antonelli, both by decreasing expectations at his home event, and also by serving the penalty while he retains a significant lead at the top of the standings.

Antonelli leads both his Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points, with McLaren's Lando Norris 83 points back in fourth after winning the last two races.

Antonelli added: "Of course, the goal is always the same and we're going to try and maximise the result.

"In an ideal world, I think realistically top five you can do well. But it's all driven also by your pace, how fast you are. What's the gap between cars? We might be really quick but Ferrari or McLaren or Red Bull they might be very close that it's not enough to catch them during the race.

"We'll see but I feel very free mentally going into this weekend. Very excited, very much looking forward to it, but with no real pressure."
